title: Rate-limiting a hook that runs on every prompt

concepts.description: A cooldown limits how often something fires; a hard cap limits how many times it can fire at all, which is what bounds a condition that never resolves.
concepts.context: MAX_NUDGES bounds the nudge because 'this session logged nothing' is also what an unreachable MCP server looks like from inside the hook

concepts.description: Storing small per-entity state as pipe- or JSON-delimited values in a generic key/value table, trading query power for not needing a migration.
concepts.context: the nudge keeps `<first-seen>|<last-nudge>|<count>` in one meta row rather than adding a table

concepts.description: Ordering guard clauses so the cheapest test that can exit early runs first, when the code path is hot.
concepts.context: config is read before SQLite is opened, because this hook runs on every prompt the developer types
